text: [{"id":0,"latex":"Reasoning sometimes changes how things seem to us. But there is also a way things seem to us prior to reasoning; otherwise, reasoning could not get started. The way things seem prior to reasoning we may call an 'initial appearance'. An initial, intellectual appearance is an 'intuition'. That is, an intuition that $p$ is a state of its seeming to one that $p$ that is not dependent on inference from other beliefs and that results from thinking about $p$, as opposed to perceiving, remembering, or introspecting. An ethical intuition is an intuition whose content is an evaluative proposition."},{"id":1,"latex":"If $A$ is better than $B$ and $B$ is better than $C$, then $A$ is better than $C$. It is unjust to punish a person for a crime he did not commit."}]
